cost_drivers.detail: School holidays, Christmas and New Year carry the highest demand of the year. The same itinerary in a shoulder week is a different proposition entirely.
The newest ships command a premium over older tonnage sailing similar routes. If facilities matter less to you than the destination, an older class often delivers the same itinerary.
Interior to balcony is usually the single biggest step in the fare. Neighbourhood balconies sit between the two.
Cost per night often falls as sailings get longer, so a 7-night can be better value per day than a 4-night.
Gratuities, drinks, wi-fi, speciality dining and excursions can meaningfully change the all-in total. Compare the total, not the fare.
Cabin categories sell out unevenly. Accessible and connecting cabins in particular go early regardless of the calendar.

faqs.q: Which Royal Caribbean ship is best for young children?
faqs.a: The newer and larger classes carry the deepest children's facilities, bigger waterparks, more kids' club capacity with tighter age bands, and more connecting cabin options. The right answer still depends on your children's ages and how long you want to sail, which is why this is worth two minutes on the phone.

faqs.q: What is a neighbourhood balcony and should I book one?
faqs.a: On the largest classes some balconies face inward over Central Park or the Boardwalk rather than the sea. They cost less than an ocean balcony. Some travellers love the atmosphere and the shelter; others find them enclosed and noisy above the Boardwalk. Decide deliberately rather than by price.

faqs.q: Do the biggest ships feel crowded?
faqs.a: They carry more passengers but also far more venues and deck space, so density varies by design and by how you use the ship. Classes with strong neighbourhood separation tend to feel less busy than the headline capacity suggests.

faqs.q: Is a drinks package worth buying?
faqs.a: It depends entirely on how much you actually drink, and packages generally must be bought for all adults in a cabin. The maths is simple once someone walks you through it honestly, which a specialist can do in a couple of minutes.

cost_drivers.detail: Driving instead of flying removes the largest single variable for most families. Compare drive-to ports before anything else.
Short 3-5 night sailings cost less overall but more per night. Seven nights is often better value per day.
Newer classes command a premium over older tonnage sailing similar routes.
Interior to balcony is the biggest single step. Cove balconies sit in between on some ships.
Holiday weeks are the busiest and most expensive of the year.
Gratuities, drinks packages, speciality dining and excursions change the all-in total substantially.

faqs.q: Is Carnival only for young party crowds?
faqs.a: Not uniformly. Short weekend sailings draw the liveliest crowds; longer itineraries and off-peak dates attract a broader mix including families and older travellers. Choosing the right sailing length matters more than choosing the right ship.

faqs.q: Why are so many people driving to their cruise?
faqs.a: Carnival sails from more US home ports than any other line, including several that competitors ignore. For a family of four, removing four airfares changes the entire budget, worth checking before you assume you need to fly.

faqs.q: What is a cove balcony?
faqs.a: A balcony set lower in the hull, closer to the waterline and more sheltered than a standard balcony. Only some ships have them. It's a distinctive option most booking sites won't explain to you.

faqs.q: Is Holland America genuinely better for Alaska?
faqs.a: It is one of the longest-operating lines in the region with established glacier access and integrated land programmes. Whether it beats alternatives for your trip depends on your dates, budget and whether you want a land extension.

faqs.q: What is a cruisetour?
faqs.a: A one-way sailing combined with an inland land programme travelling by rail and coach toward the interior national park. More moving parts than a standard cruise, which is why most travellers arrange it by phone.

faqs.q: Is the average passenger older?
faqs.a: Generally yes, particularly on longer voyages and off-peak dates. Alaska summer sailings and holiday periods draw a broader mix.

faqs.q: What exactly is an infinite verandah?
faqs.a: A cabin design where the living space extends to the ship's edge with a retractable upper window, rather than a separate outdoor balcony. Some travellers prefer it; others miss a traditional open balcony. Understand which you're booking.

faqs.q: How is Celebrity different from mainstream lines?

faqs.q: Is suite class worth it?

faqs.q: Why do people choose Princess for Alaska?
faqs.a: The line pairs one-way sailings with rail-based land tours reaching the interior national park. Assembling that independently is difficult, which is why most travellers book it by phone.

faqs.q: Is Princess good for families?
faqs.a: It works well for multi-generation groups travelling together, but it isn't built around children the way family-focused lines are. If children are the primary consideration, other lines offer more.

faqs.q: What does the wearable device actually do?
faqs.a: Boarding, cabin access, onboard payments and locating your party. It's more useful with a large group, set it up before boarding rather than at the terminal.

faqs.q: What is a transatlantic crossing actually like?
faqs.a: Roughly a week of open ocean between New York and Southampton with no port calls. Days are filled with lectures, dancing, dining and the sea. Travellers either find it deeply restorative or extremely long, there's little middle ground.

faqs.q: How formal is it really?
faqs.a: More formal than any other mainstream line. Gala evenings carry real expectations and most passengers observe them enthusiastically. If dressing for dinner sounds like a burden, another line suits you better.

faqs.q: Does cabin grade really affect dining?
faqs.a: Yes, your cabin grade determines your restaurant assignment, with suite guests in separate dining rooms. This makes cabin choice more consequential here than on any other line.

cost_drivers.detail: Sailings over the school holidays are the busiest weeks of the year on a family line, and they price accordingly.
A family of five needs a cabin that sleeps five, and on any ship those are a small part of the inventory. The constraint is availability, not just fare.
Two connecting cabins can work out differently from one larger one. Worth pricing both ways for your dates.

faqs.q: How young can a baby be to sail?
faqs.a: Disney's US terms set the minimum at 6 months on most itineraries, and 1 year on Transatlantic, Hawaii, Panama Canal and other select longer sailings. Call and we will confirm which rule applies to the exact sailing you are looking at.

faqs.q: Are gratuities included in the fare?
faqs.a: No. Disney's terms list gratuities as excluded from the cruise fare and added to your onboard account, and they can be adjusted on board. We have not yet verified the current per-night amount from an official Disney page, so we show it as a gap rather than guess.

faqs.q: Which ships are in the fleet?
faqs.a: Disney's own fleet page currently names nine: Disney Adventure, Believe, Destiny, Dream, Fantasy, Magic, Treasure, Wish and Wonder. It publishes no tonnage or guest capacity, so our ship pages show those as gaps.

lines.name: Norwegian
lines.one_line: Big ships run without fixed dining times or a formal dress code, from more US home ports than almost any other line.

company._note: Fleet size is a count of the ships Norwegian's own fleet page lists. Founding year, headquarters and parent company are not stated on the pages we read, so they are gaps. Do not fill them from a holding-company figure: Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings reports a combined fleet across three brands, which is not this line's fleet.

family.age_bands: Splash Academy ages 3 to 12; Entourage ages 13 to 17
family._note: Norwegian's own FAQ sets registration at 3 for Splash Academy and 13 for Entourage. A separate Guppies open-play session is referenced for younger children but the pages conflict on whether drop-off is offered, so we state only the two we verified.

accessibility.tender_port_note: Some ports are reached by tender, a small boat that ferries guests ashore from a ship at anchor. itineraries._note: The 15 ports Norwegian's own Cruise Ports page labels United States. San Juan is also a departure port but the page labels it Puerto Rico, so it is listed separately there and we have not merged it in. Deployment rotates; re-check each season.

editorial._note: Our own words throughout, never the line's.
who_its_for: Travellers who do not want an assigned dining time
Anyone sailing from a port closer to home than Florida
Groups who want to eat and do different things on the same night
First-time cruisers who dislike formal nights
who_its_not_for: Anyone who wants a fixed table and the same waiter all week
Travellers who prefer a small ship
Guests who want everything bundled into one fare with no add-ons to decide on

cost_drivers.detail: Norwegian sells its drinks, dining, wifi and excursion perks as a package attached to the fare. Whether you take it, and which tier, moves the total more than the cabin does on a short sailing.

A daily onboard service charge is added per guest and varies by stateroom category. We have not yet verified the current US amount from Norwegian's US page, so we show it as a gap rather than publish a figure from another market.
The same ship and the same week can cost very differently depending on which of 15 US ports you sail from, once you add the flights to get there.

faqs.q: Do I have to eat at a set time?
faqs.a: No. Norwegian's format has no fixed dining time or assigned table in the main dining rooms. Specialty restaurants are bookable and carry a cover.

faqs.q: Which US ports does Norwegian sail from?
faqs.a: Norwegian's own Cruise Ports page lists 15 US departure ports: Boston, Galveston, Honolulu, Jacksonville, Los Angeles, Miami, New Orleans, New York, Orlando (Port Canaveral), Philadelphia, San Diego, San Francisco, Seattle, Tampa and Whittier. San Juan is also a departure port. Which ships sail from where changes by season.

faqs.q: How big are the ships?
faqs.a: Guest capacity runs from about 1,878 on Norwegian Sun to about 4,218 on Norwegian Escape, at double occupancy. Norwegian does not publish gross tonnage on its ship pages, so we show that as a gap rather than repeat a figure we cannot source.

editorial._note: Our own words throughout, never the line's.
who_its_for: Adults who want a sailing with no children on board
Couples and friend groups
Solo travellers, who have cabins built and priced for one
Anyone who would rather the tips and the wifi were already paid

cost_drivers.factor: What is already in the fare
cost_drivers.detail: Tips, wifi, the restaurants and the fitness classes are included, so compare this line against another by total trip cost rather than by fare alone.

The gap between an Insider with no window and a Sea Terrace with a balcony is the single biggest decision on these ships, since 86 per cent of cabins have a terrace and the few that do not sell differently.

cost_drivers.factor: Sailing from Miami or New York
cost_drivers.detail: Only two of the four ships are in US waters at any one time, so the date you want may only exist from one coast.

faqs.q: Can children sail?
faqs.a: No. The line states the minimum age to book and sail is 18 years old, and describes the ships as exclusively adult. There is no children's programming on board.

faqs.q: Are tips really included?
faqs.a: The line's own media fact sheet says all gratuities are covered in the voyage fare, along with dining at more than 20 eateries, wifi, essential drinks and unlimited group fitness classes. Alcohol, specialty drinks, shore excursions and the spa cost extra.

faqs.q: Is there a cabin for one person?
faqs.a: Yes. Solo Insider cabins are designed and priced for a single traveller, which is unusual and worth asking about, because the alternative on most lines is paying a supplement for a double cabin.

faqs.q: Which ships sail from the US?
faqs.a: The fact sheet has Valiant Lady from PortMiami on four- and five-night Caribbean and Mexico itineraries, and Brilliant Lady debuting from New York. Scarlet Lady and Resilient Lady spend part of the year in Europe and return to Miami for the winter. Call and we will confirm which ship is where for your dates.

company._note: Fleet size is a count of the ships with a page under costacruises.com/fleet/. Costa's own company page times out for our fetcher, so founding year, headquarters, parent company and its own published fleet size are gaps. Fill them from that page when it loads, not from a third party.

cost_drivers.detail: With no US home port, the flights are part of the real cost of a Costa cruise and can exceed the cruise fare on a short sailing.
Mediterranean sailings are priced very differently in August and in November for the same ship and the same route.

faqs.q: Can I sail Costa from a US port?
faqs.a: No. Costa has no United States departure port, so a Costa cruise means flying to the ship. If you want an Italian-style ship sailing from the US, call and we will point you at the lines that do.

faqs.q: Which ships are in the fleet?
faqs.a: Eight have a page on Costa's own site: Costa Deliziosa, Favolosa, Firenze, Fortuna, Serena, Smeralda, Toscana and Venezia. Costa publishes no tonnage or guest capacity on those pages, so our ship pages show those as gaps.

editorial._note: Our own words throughout, never the line's.
who_its_for: Travellers who want a ship measured in hundreds of guests rather than thousands
Anyone who would rather pay once and not sign for drinks all week
Guests going somewhere a large ship cannot, on the expedition ships
Repeat cruisers who have done the big-ship lines
who_its_not_for: Families looking for children's programming
Anyone who wants waterslides, a casino floor and a theatre show every night
Travellers booking on fare alone, since these are the most expensive ships we cover

cost_drivers.factor: Which fare the sailing is sold under
cost_drivers.detail: Silversea sells several fares and the difference between them is mostly whether shore excursions and flights are in or out. Two quotes for the same voyage can be comparing different things.
The expedition ships carry 100 to 274 guests and go where the classic ships do not. They are priced on where they go, not on what is on board.
Every cabin is a suite with a butler, so the decision is about size and position rather than whether you get a window.

faqs.q: Are drinks and tips included?
faqs.a: On the All-Inclusive fare, yes. The line's own fare page lists onboard gratuities, an in-suite bar, unlimited pours of champagne and spirits, up to 50 wines from the ship's cellar, wifi and port taxes. It states that fare is available on Classic voyages.

faqs.q: Are shore excursions included?
faqs.a: It depends which fare the sailing is sold under, and this is the detail that catches people out. On the All-Inclusive fare, excursions are bought separately. Other Silversea fares include them. Call and we will have a partner agency confirm which fare applies to the voyage you are looking at.

faqs.q: How big are the ships?
faqs.a: The classic ships carry 392 to 728 guests and the four expedition ships carry 100 to 274, per the line's own ships page. Silversea publishes crew numbers alongside, which is unusual and tells you more about the service than tonnage would.
